title: Laser / toner — what the decoupage method wants
note: Toner is fused plastic sitting on the paper surface, so water-based Mod Podge goes over it without bleeding. Ask for colour laser, 100% scale, plain or lightweight paper — thin paper conforms to the tile better than cardstock. Most high-street copy shops, office-supply chains and shipping stores can do this while you wait, and it is cheap enough to reprint a sheet when a tile goes wrong. Use the search above to find one near you.

title: Fine-art inkjet — richer colour, but sacrifice a test tile
note: Giclée studios print with pigment inkjet. Colour depth beats toner noticeably on paintings, and pigment ink is far more water-fast than dye — but it is still inkjet under water-based glue. Print one extra square, decoupage it onto a spare tile, and let it cure before committing the rest. Sealing the print with a light clear acrylic spray before gluing helps a lot.

title: Skip the craft — order finished coasters
note: If you would rather not do the glue-and-seal cycle, these take an exported square and ship back a finished cork-backed coaster. Upload the full-coverage export rather than the bordered one.
